name: Step Tick - Commit Refused
description: What happens when a tick cannot be saved. The isolation page pins a signed-in session but holds no GitHub token, so the commit is refused — which makes this the honest capture of the failure path rather than a mocked approximation of it. The box shows the change optimistically, the commit fails, and the box goes BACK, with the reason stated. That revert is the behaviour worth pinning down: a checkbox that stays ticked after a failed commit is a lie the next reader has no way to detect, and on a page whose entire value is that what it shows is what everyone else sees, a silent local-only tick would be worse than no checkbox at all.
